1.explanation:
• ComboBox.js is the heart of the violation: it uses Downshift and manually concatenates the input id + "__menu" for aria-owns/aria-controls and wires getInputProps/getRootProps. DAP is complaining that those IDs either don’t exist on the referenced element or aren’t valid per ARIA spec.  
• ListBoxField.js renders the <button> wrapper for the combobox toggle. It never applies an aria-label or aria-labelledby that ties back to the visible labelText, so DAP flags the interactive element as unnamed.  
• ListBoxMenu.js renders the <div id="{id}__menu" role="listbox"> for the menu. Because its id doesn’t match the aria-owns/aria-controls from ComboBox.js, or because it isn’t rendered at the time of the check, DAP reports an invalid reference.  

Fixing the bug will require:  
1. Ensuring the menu container’s id exactly matches what the input and listbox root reference in aria-controls/aria-owns.  
2. Moving any visually-hidden inputs into a proper region (or suppressing the extra Downshift input) so they aren’t flagged as floating outside a landmark.  
3. Adding an aria-label or aria-labelledby to the toggle button in ListBoxField that matches the visible labelText passed into ComboBox.  
4. Verifying that all IDs conform to the ARIA spec (no illegal characters, no duplicates) and line up with the generated attributes at runtime.
1.bug_scenario:
When you run the Carbon React ComboBox examples under DAP, you get multiple WAI-ARIA violations:

1. “The id specified for WAI-ARIA property aria-owns/aria-controls on element is not valid” – the menu container’s id (e.g. carbon-combobox-example__menu) doesn’t match what DAP expects (or isn’t being rendered by the same element reference).  
2. An interactive element/widget must have an accessible name – the toggle button that wraps the text input has no name or label.  
3. All content must reside within a WAI-ARIA landmark or labelled region role – the visually hidden input that Downshift injects is floating outside any region or landmark.  
4. Accessible name does not contain the visible label text – the combobox’s visible labelText is never tied into the aria-label or aria-labelledby on the interactive portion of the combobox.  

All of these issues originate in how ComboBox builds its aria-* attributes and IDs (in ComboBox.js) and how the ListBox pieces (ListBoxField, ListBoxMenu) provide roles, IDs, and labels.

2.explanation:
• ComboBox.js is responsible for rendering the wrapper <div>, the <input> (with aria-controls) and the listbox trigger (with aria-owns). The missing role="combobox" on the wrapper, lack of aria-labelledby to tie in the visible label, and the injection of aria-controls on the wrong element all stem from this file.

• ListBox.js is where the <div role="listbox"> wrapper is defined. Its static role assignment and id propagation via getRootProps currently do not align with the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern; this is why DAP marks the id references as invalid and flags missing naming.

• ListBoxMenu.js generates the menu container’s id (``${id}__menu``) and sets role="listbox" on it. That id is the target of aria-owns/aria-controls. Because the pattern is out of compliance, the id being referenced is rejected by DAP. Adjusting id generation or how aria-owns / aria-controls get wired up here is required to resolve the violation.
2.bug_scenario:
When running the Carbon React ComboBox example through DAP (Accessibility Insights), several ARIA violations are reported. The two most prominent errors are:

1. “The id identifier specified for WAI-ARIA property identifier on element identifier is not valid.”
   • aria-owns on the outer container references “carbon-combobox-example__menu” (generated by ListBoxMenu) but DAP flags that id as invalid
   • aria-controls on the <input> also points at “carbon-combobox-example__menu” and is similarly flagged

2. The composite combobox widget has no accessible name or landmark role, and the visible label (titleText) is not used in its accessible name. The wrapper <div> around the control has no role="combobox" or aria-labelledby, so the widget is not recognized as a combobox by assistive tools.

In the screenshot you can see the input and its listbox rendering correctly, but the developer tools’ DAP panel calls out invalid id references and missing accessible naming and roles.
